Start here

From nothing to a site whose members sign in, in order.

1. Make your community

At wallflowers.io/signup: what it is, its name and its address, then, if you are building an app, Your app (its local port, callback path and deployed URL; or Skip), then your account. You are its owner. Already have a WallFlowers account? Press Create my account, then, on the next page, choose Sign in with a passkey, so the community is made for the account you already have.

With Your app filled in, signup brings you back after you register and lists your community's Site id, Address, Client and Callback and, for a deployed URL, the request to send, each with Copy.

Keep your passkey safe. Save it in a synced password manager, or on your phone: a phone's passkey signs you in on any laptop, through the browser's option to use a phone (a QR code). A lost passkey can't be recovered on the web today: it means a new account.

2. Build on your machine

Make your community first, at wallflowers.io/signup, before you run the starter: you will own it. Signing up from the starter instead makes an account with no community, and its sign-in stops at "you are the owner or an admin of no Site". If that happened, make the community at signup, press Create my account, and on the next page choose Sign in with a passkey with that account.

Then nothing to register: use the shared client hackathon-local on localhost, and follow the Quickstart. When you sign in, pick your community (On your machine).

3. Put it on the web

Your site needs an https address. A hosting service gives you one; for a domain of your own, buy one at Spaceship and point it at your host. Then register that exact origin and its callback page (Register your app). A registration counts within seconds of WallFlowers adding it: the Door reads its list of sites again every 2 s, with no restart, so no one is signed out. It does not change the sign-in script or its hash.

Building with an app builder (Lovable, v0, Bolt)

  • If it lets you edit the page's code, add the sign-in script with its integrity, and make the calls as the Quickstart does.
  • Sign in with your app open in its own tab. WallFlowers' sign-in window refuses to be shown inside a frame, and an editor's preview is a frame.
  • The preview's address and the published one are different origins: register each one you sign in from. hackathon-local covers only your own machine.
  • Builders may add scripts of their own to your page (a badge, analytics). Anything on the page can use the member's session, so on pages where members sign in, keep only what you need (Your page's rules).
